text: When you ask ChatGPT a question, how does it come up with its answer?
reference_answer: It predicts the next word (token) again and again, based on patterns it learned from a huge amount of text during training. It does not look the answer up, and it can sound confident even when it is wrong.

text: A spam filter scores 99% accuracy on the emails it was trained on, but only 60% on new emails. What most likely went wrong?
reference_answer: The model overfit: it memorized details of the training emails instead of learning general patterns, so it does not work well on emails it has not seen. Testing on held-out data catches this.

text: An AI hiring tool rejects more women than men, even though it was never given anyone's gender. How can this happen?
reference_answer: The model learned from past hiring data that was already biased. Other features, like hobbies, clubs or word choice in a resume, can act as stand-ins for gender, so the model repeats the old bias.
